items.title: America’s Trillion-Dollar Credit Card Debt Threatens To Lock Millions Out of the Housing Market
items.description: With prices still alarmingly high, it comes as no surprise that Americans are increasingly turning to credit cards more than ever. But doing so could be silently sabotaging any hope of owning a home , if you’re not careful. Last week, the Federal Reserve Bank of New York published its latest household debt report . Collectively, credit card balances climbed by $22 billion in the third quarter to a record $1.29 trillion. Balances are up 4.2% from a year earlier, and total household debt, including mortgages, auto loans, and student loans, expanded by $334 billion for the period to a record $19.1 trillion. High levels of debt are problematic for anyone, but most especially for first-time homebuyers. If your ambitions for 2027 include buying a home, it’s important to get your debt in check before it’s too late. Easy money comes at a price According to TransUnion’s most recent quarterly credit industry insights report , the number of people with credit cards rose 2% to 178 million up from 174.8 million. The ease of use means most people turn to credit cards for their everyday purchases, like groceries, gas, and utility bills—all of which have seen a steep increase in prices over the past two years. Now, if you’re someone who pays off their credit card in full each month, you’re in the clear. If not, the average interest rate on a new credit card offer currently stands at about 24%, and debt can accumulate quickly. And this can cause an array of issues for first-time homebuyers. "Issues arising from high levels of consumer debt are amplified for first-time homebuyers as they typically have less savings, limited financial history, and tighter financial conditions,” John Donikian , vice president of Best Interest Financial in West Bloomfield, MI , tells Realtor.com® . Loading... Credit card debt is nothing to ignore, especially if you're hoping to buy a home. Getty Images The problem with carrying too much credit card debt Firstly, carrying too much debt can negatively affect your credit score , a vital metric in getting a mortgage. While there is no firm number to qualify for a mortgage, a good credit score ranges from 700 to 749, and most conventional loans typically require at least 620. Lenders may accept lower scores if you have a larger down payment or other strong financial factors. The higher your balances are, the more your score is dragged down, which can not only affect the interest rate a lender can offer you, but also keep you from getting a mortgage with some lenders entirely. “Your credit score doesn’t just determine if you are approved; it influences your interest rate and the monthly payment you are offered,” says Jake Vehige , president of mortgage lending at Neighbors Bank. “Even a small difference in interest rates can add up to thousands of dollars over the life of a loan.” Secondly, as part of the process of getting a mortgage, lenders will look at your debt-to-income ratio to see how much house you can afford. If a lender looks at your total monthly debt payments against your gross monthly income and your DTI exceeds its caps, your application could be delayed or even denied outright. But both of those instances can be reversed, with time and a fixed budget that allows you to pay off your debt. In other words, your credit score can rebound. Where first-time buyers are really at a disadvantage by accumulating so much credit card debt is the drain it will put on their savings. The money that you’ll need to rack up to pay off the 20%-plus interest on your bills could have been money saved for your down payment, closing costs, and repair funds. Many lenders also require proof of postclosing cash reserves, which is much harder to build while paying down high-interest debt. “Ideally, you want to keep your credit card balances at no more than 20% to 30% of your maximum credit limit," explains Jeremy Schachter , branch manager at Fairway Independent Mortgage Corp. in Phoenix . "For example, if you have a $1,000 limit, don’t go over a balance higher than $200 to $300. Anything that exceeds that amount can lower your credit score and make it difficult to get approved for a mortgage with a good rate.” Dina Sartore-Bodo is the senior editor at Realtor.com covering real estate news, personal finance trends, and interior design. She previously served as the managing editor at HollywoodLife.com, the executive editor at PerezHilton.com, and as a managing editor at Mediavine. Her work has also appeared on MSN, Yahoo News, and BlogHer. She is a proud graduate of Emerson College in Boston and is originally from New Jersey.

items.title: Blackstone's Data Center REIT Makes First Investment With $5B AWS Deal
items.description: Blackstone ’s recently listed data center acquisition business made its first purchase, a $5B stake in Amazon -leased data centers. Unsplash/Scott Rodgerson Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust is acquiring a 75% majority stake in two joint ventures with Amazon Web Services to acquire 13 newly constructed powered shells across two AWS campuses in a deal valued at $5B, the investment management giant announced Monday . Amazon will lease back 100% of the portfolio from the REIT, which trades under the ticker BXDC, on a triple-net basis with an initial term of 12 years and an option to expand the length to 32 years. Rent payments are guaranteed by AWS, according to a presentation published with the announcement. The inaugural acquisition for the REIT comes at a 7.0% capitalization rate. Two-thirds of the portfolio is in the greater Chicago region with the remainder in Mississippi. “The quality, basis and tenant profile of these assets make this an attractive match for the deployment of our IPO proceeds,” BXDC CEO Nick Pell said in a statement. “Given the deep expertise across our platform, we believe BXDC is well positioned to capitalize on a highly compelling opportunity and deliver value for our shareholders.” The transaction is expected to close before the end of the year. Blackstone launched the public REIT in May . The business is seeking newly constructed but stabilized data centers occupied by “top investment-grade hyperscalers ” valued between $250B and $1.5B. BXDC is targeting returns between 5.75% and 7% or more, according to a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission . Blackstone has been one of the most active backers of artificial intelligence infrastructure like data centers and power facilities through its Blackstone Energy Transition Partners. It was early to the data center race, agreeing in 2021 to acquire QTS Realty Trust at a $10B valuation . The investment giant’s flagship private real estate fund, Blackstone Real Estate Income Trust , deployed $3.4B into preleased data center development through QTS in the third quarter, bringing its year-to-date deployment to the sector to roughly $9B. Shares in BXDC were up more than 7% in premarket trading following the announcement of the deal with AWS but gave up some of those gains at the opening bell. items.description: A 346-unit apartment complex, part of the first phase of a mixed-use development in Houston’s Spring Branch, is nearing completion. Courtesy of Arch-Con Corp. The Springs tops out at 1235 Shadowdale Drive in Houston's Silo Falls mixed-use development. Moody National Cos. topped out on the five-story, 364K SF multifamily building called The Springs, general contractor Arch-Con Corp. announced Monday. The Springs is at 1235 Shadowdale Drive in Silo Falls, a 17-acre mixed-use development on the site of the long-vacant historic Shadowdale grain silos. Along with the ground-up construction of the complex, the initial phase of Silo Falls includes refreshing the concrete silos with paint, lighting and signage. Moody National plans to install a water feature on the 132-foot-tall structures in hopes of competing with The Galleria ’s Waterwall, the Houston Chronicle reported . items.title: Lenders increasingly pull with new credit score model, but few use it for pricing
items.description: Mortgage lenders are frequently pulling credit scores with VantageScore 4.0, but most of them still price with Classic FICO , according to a new Bank of America Global Research report based on Recursion data. The report, released on Friday, shows that Rocket Mortgage and United Wholesale Mortgage (UWM) are driving nearly all of the production actually priced with the new scoring model in the agency mortgage-backed securities (MBS) market. Since October, Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac have required that agency MBS pools disclose both Classic FICO and VantageScore 4.0 whenever both are pulled, and to identify which score was used for pricing. According to Bank of America, 148 sellers in October delivered agency MBS loans for which a VS4 score had been pulled. That figure rose to 173 sellers during the first 10 days of November. But the number of lenders actually pricing loans with VS4 remains much smaller. Only eight lenders sold loans priced with VS4 in September, which rose to 22 in October and 37 to date in November. In October, 20% of conventional issuance reported a VS4 score, BofA said. Of that subset, 39% used VS4 as the pricing score, which works out to roughly 8% of total conventional issuance. Most of these loans had both scores: 18% of issuance reported both FICO and VS4 , while only 2% reported VS4 alone. Thus far in November, 21% of issuance had VS4 reported and 32% of these loans used VS4 for pricing, or about 7% of total issuance. Early adopters Rocket and UWM are the main early adopters on the pricing side. In October, BofA found that Rocket and UWM together accounted for 65% of all loans with a VS4 score pulled. They also were the sources for 95% of loans that used VS4 as their pricing score in the agency MBS market. Among other lenders that have shown they can pull VS4, just 13% of their production had a VS4 score reported and only 1% of loans actually used VS4 to set prices. “We think this disconnect largely reflects a gradual ramp-up in operational and infrastructure readiness,” BofA analysts said. “Pulling and reporting an additional score is relatively straightforward, while actually incorporating VS4 into loan pricing likely requires more extensive changes to lenders' pricing systems and operational infrastructure.” BofA’s report also notes that loans priced with VS4 have distinctive collateral characteristics. VS4-priced loans tend to have higher average loan balances , a lower share of first-time homebuyers , and higher shares of cash-out and rate-and-term refinance loans. Among VS4-priced loans where both scores were reported, the VS4 score was on average about 43 points higher than FICO. For FICO-priced loans with both scores present, the two models are broadly comparable, the analysts said. Because lenders can choose between scores when both are present, the emerging “best-of-two” selection framework is affecting the distribution of published scores. BofA found that among October loans with both scores reported, 24% had FICO scores below 700 and 21% had VS4 scores below 700, but only 17% had a pricing score below 700. Potential refis BofA also addressed investor concerns that borrowers in legacy low-FICO pools who have materially higher VS4 scores could see a one-time chance to refinance as markets and pricing grids adjust to VS4. “We acknowledge that legacy low-FICO pools are exposed to this risk,” the analysts said. “However, newly issued low credit score pools may offer a way to mitigate this risk and potentially access even better convexity collateral.” According to the report, low credit score pool collateral today generally consists of loans that either have both FICO and VS4 reported with both scores below 700, or are VS4-only loans. Loans with both FICO and VS4 below 700 have already been screened against the risk that a significantly higher VS4 score would give borrowers a one-time refinancing opportunity. Additionally, a historical analysis indicates that loans with both scores below 700 exhibit better convexity than loans defined only by FICOs below 700. Related More: Credit Score FICO VantageScore

items.title: Why database touch plans fail real estate agents
items.description: Agents are consistently trained to do their touches. "Have you done all your touches?" "Have you done your outreach?" "Are you touching people?" "Are you sending things of value?" That antiquated philosophy needs to stop and almost nobody in this industry cares to address it or examine why it fails. It is wildly ineffective, and I would argue that most of the time it hurts the agent's brand rather than helping it. If I walked up to your front door 32 times a year, rang the bell, and said, "Just a reminder that I'm in real estate," how long would it take you to look into a restraining order? Nobody would call that a relationship. Yet the same schedule applies when it arrives as an email one week and a postcard the next. Agents are constantly told they need to remind people that they are in real estate. That is an interaction about what the agent cares about, not what the other person cares about. Trust isn't built by constantly telling someone how amazing I am, why they need me, or why I'm relevant or important. That is blatant narcissism, and yet somehow we call it great top-of-mind marketing. Why happy clients still hire someone else The National Association of Realtors' 2025 Profile of Home Buyers and Sellers shows the problem. Ninety-one percent of buyers said they would use their agent again or recommend them. But among repeat buyers, only 18% went back to an agent they had worked with before , and among sellers the figure was 29%. The touches are supposed to close that gap. The industry explains that clients forget, so its answer has always been more reminders—the rest of the survey points somewhere else. 80% of sellers contacted only one agent before hiring, and 66% hired someone referred to them or someone they had used before. Sellers are not comparing the agents who emailed or mailed them the most. They call the one person they trust. Seeing your name in their inbox every month does not make you that person. One of the agents I coach has phenomenal email automation, with reminders and alerts set up for everyone they have ever worked with. By their own count, 90% of their business comes from less than 5% of the people in their database . If 90% of your business comes from less than 5% of those people, why are you digitally harassing the other 95%? We can keep up with about 150 people In 2003, researchers Russell Hill and Robin Dunbar measured how many people we keep up with by using the most ordinary list there is, the one for Christmas cards. Participants logged every card they sent and everyone in the household it went to. Networks averaged about 150 people, and participants stayed in touch weekly with the people they felt closest to. A later study by Sam Roberts and Dunbar followed people for 18 months. Friendships lost closeness when contact dropped off, while family relationships were far less affected. Contact matters, and the touch plans are right about that much. They go wrong by treating a Christmas card to the whole database as the same act as staying close to 150. A mailing treats everyone alike, so the people who matter most get the same thing as the strangers, and the relationships that produce business fade. What to do instead Pick your 150. Write down the people you would be glad to call and stop when you reach that number. They will be past clients and friends whose lives you know something about. Dunbar's later research found an inner circle of about 15 inside the 150. Give those 15 their own rhythm, a conversation with each of them every month, because in my experience that inner circle is where most referrals come from. A database you can't keep up with starts to feel like a weight. A list of 150 is small enough that you notice when one of them is about to move. Reconnect at four months. A conversation creates what I call mind share: the trust that comes from talking with someone. Name recognition never builds it, and without the next conversation it fades. In my coaching, I see it run low about three to four months after the last conversation. Once a week, scroll back about four months in your text messages, pick three people, and send something like "Hey, was just thinking about you. Hope all is well; would love to catch up." Leave real estate out of it. Anyone in your text messages already has a relationship with you that a mailing list never will, so the message reaches someone who trusts you at the point where that trust is lowest. Keep it to three. Send 30, have 10 people answer and your afternoon is gone, which is the fastest way to make sure you never do it again. If you lead agents, ask how many conversations they had with their 150 this month, not how many touches they made. That number tells you whose relationships are fading before the referrals stop. We keep overcomplicating this business by pushing agents to do more and more, which only creates overwhelm and makes them more likely to do less. We owe them better. Lance Pendleton is the founder of PreTSD Consulting and the creator of Reframe Lab. He was previously National Head of Agent Development at Compass and Chief Innovation Officer for the largest Sotheby’s International Realty affiliate in the US. items.title: The Tuccori commission settlements were supposed to wrap up, then the judge asked for more
items.description: Many real estate industry players were hoping to head into the holiday season with homebuyer commission lawsuit claims squarely in the rearview mirror, but that is not how the expected final approval hearing for the Tuccori commission lawsuit settlements played out. At a hearing earlier this month, the court decided it needed a closer look at how the settlements and opt-in settlements came to be before issuing a final ruling. The settlements in question include those reached by the National Association of Realtors ($52.25 million), Compass ($7.33 million), eXp World Holdings ($4.34 million), Hanna Holdings ($8.25), HomeServices of America ($30 million) and Douglas Elliman ($2.04 million). Like many of the defendants that settled via the Tuccori opt-in option, these parties were originally named as defendants in the Batton 1 and 2 , Cwynar , Davis and Lutz lawsuits. In an order earlier this month, the judge created a list of things the court would like further information on before issuing its ruling on the settlements. Much of the information focuses on how the settlement amounts were determined and whether they are fair to settlement class members. Specifically, the court is seeking clarification on whether previous home seller settlements are an appropriate benchmark for the buyer settlements, given that those agreements resolved both buyer and seller claims. She also wants to understand how each settling defendant’s or opt-in’s financial ability to pay and transaction volume factored into its settlement amount, and what plaintiffs could realistically expect to recover if they continued litigating and went to trial. Additionally, the judge is asking the parties to provide examples of settlement benchmarks from other indirect purchaser class actions and to estimate how much individual claimants and class members would actually receive under the proposed settlements. The settling parties have until Dec. 14, 2026, to submit briefs addressing these five topics. After reviewing these briefs, the court said it will then consider if further responses are necessary. This outcome is certainly a blow to the suit’s numerous real estate brokerage defendants, as well as NAR. In an emailed statement a spokesperson for the NAR told HousingWire that the trade group "continues to believe the Tuccori settlement is fair, reasonable, and in the best interests of the class. "The court’s ongoing review is a standard part of the settlement approval process, and we remain confident in the meaningful protections the settlement offers across the industry, including a broad release for Realtor members, Realtor associations, MLSs, and those brokerages that meet the settlement’s eligibility requirements," the spokesperson added. "NAR remains committed to fostering fair, transparent, and pro-consumer real estate markets while providing resources and value to our Realtor members nationwide.” The opt-in settlements, which total over $120 million, gained preliminary approval in late May . At this hearing, the court rejected the claims that these settlements were the result of a “ reverse auction ,” instead finding that the proposed opt-in settlements were “fair, reasonable and adequate,” and that the “Opt-In Agreements compensate indirect purchaser claims at almost the same rate as the claims previously resolved by the [home seller] Burnett , Gibson, Keel and Hooper settlements.” Related More: Commission Lawsuit NAR Lawsuit Settlement National Association of Realtors

items.title: Wall Street's Big CRE Lenders Are Pulling Back While Private Credit Fights For Deals
items.description: Most of Wall Street’s biggest commercial real estate lenders are getting paid back faster than they’re lending, and their dividends are starting to crack. The public lenders are losing ground just as private credit fights hardest for deals, pushing spreads on top-quality loans tighter even after the Federal Reserve ’s September rate hike, Bisnow reported last week . The mortgage REITs piled into lending when rates were near zero, and losses on those 2021 and 2022 loans are now eating the capital they would need to compete. Analysts who spoke with Bisnow don’t expect them back in force until the middle of next year at the earliest. Blackstone Mortgage Trust cut its quarterly dividend 36% to 30 cents a share after a $327M third-quarter loss, the company reported late last month , and collected $2.3B in repayments while closing about $500M in new investments. KKR Real Estate Finance Trust got $1.2B back from borrowers and made just $157M in new loans, according to its earnings release , and its book value has fallen 26% in a year to $10.14 a share. Bisnow/created with ChatGPT Even Starwood Property Trust , which made $2.4B in commercial loans in the quarter, its most in four years, posted a $390M loss, the company reported Nov. 6 , and is weighing a cut to the 48-cent dividend it has paid for more than a decade. “It’s all blue sky for them,” BTIG Managing Director Thomas Catherwood told Bisnow of the private lenders. “Whereas the public guys are still dealing with this overhang.” Starwood CEO Barry Sternlicht said on the company’s earnings call that the dividend has been running above earnings and that the board will meet to set a new rate. “It hurts me to do anything to the dividend,” Sternlicht said. “But I think the right thing to do is navigate through this valley.” KREF has gone further, running a strategic review that could end in a sale or merger. Those legacy loans tie the REITs’ hands in a way they don’t for private funds, said Kim Golden, director of nonbank financial institutions at Fitch Ratings . REITs must pay out at least 90% of their taxable income to shareholders, so they can't rebuild capital by holding on to earnings, and impaired legacy loans are eating into the equity that supports their borrowing. “The REITs themselves are not able to [invest] while staying in their leverage levels as they kind of work through some of these impaired loans, which were originated in pre-2022,” Golden said. “A debt fund, for example, they’re not necessarily tied to that. They can raise new capital and won't be tied to these pre-2022 vintages and can continue to originate loans.” Wikimedia Commons/Christopher Michel Starwood International CEO Barry Sternlicht Not every public lender is pulling back. Catherwood said Starwood, Ladder Capital and TPG RE Finance Trust remain in growth mode because their portfolios carry less legacy baggage, even as Starwood weighs its dividend. Wall Street has already punished the rest. Mortgage REIT book values are down about 30% this cycle, and the stocks trade at 50% to 60% of book value, close to a trough, said Jade Rahmani , a managing director at Keefe, Bruyette & Woods. The market has priced in another half-point Fed hike expected in December, he said. “It’s clear to say the market is pricing in some significant losses,” Rahmani said. “Moving 50 basis points at this point is not going to be the straw that broke the camel’s back.” The next round of pain is more likely to come from apartments than offices, particularly Class-B and C properties, he said. “That risks sort of a second round of stress on these portfolios,” Rahmani said. “They seem to have dealt with their office challenges, but there are surely multifamily loans that have been modified and extended in hopes of lower rates. And now, we're facing higher rates.” Golden said slow lending is likely to continue if rates stay volatile, and some borrowers who can’t or won’t put in more equity could walk away. “I wouldn’t be surprised to see more keys coming back,” she said. Even if rates stabilize, Catherwood said a handful of public lenders will still be working through legacy loans into 2028. Another Fed hike in December would add pressure, he said, but he doesn't see it as a turning point. “I don’t think it’s a cataclysmic event,” Catherwood said. “It’s a speed bump to get through these resolutions.” Continue reading this story with a free account Log in or register Related Topics: Barry Sternlicht , Blackstone Mortgage Trust , BTIG , Kim Golden , KKR Real Estate Finance Trust , Mortgage REITs , Starwood Property Trust , Thomas Catherwood

items.title: Dutch Rental System Change Will Help Income But Won't Stop Home Decline
items.description: Changes to the Dutch housing rental system devised to give private landlords more financial breathing room are unlikely to stem the drop in private rental supply, according to Savills. From Jan. 1, 2027, adjustments to the rental points system — woningwaarderingsstelsel, or WWS — will let landlords of certain regulated homes charge higher rents while the homes stay regulated. The changes target homes affected by the cap on official property value (WOZ), self-contained homes without outdoor space, small listed homes in monumental buildings and homes with a very low WOZ value. Pexels/Jan van der Wolf The new WOZ-based surcharge could tack on several hundred euros of rent for certain midrange assets in cities with higher property value, but it will not stop the decline in private rental supply or reset the market, Savills said in its latest Spotlight report . The private rental stock shrank by about 22,000 homes in the year to Jan. 1, 2026, according to Statistics Netherlands , as private individuals’ rental holdings fell by nearly 37,000. The rental point system in the Netherlands scores a home on features such as floor space, energy label and property value. The total determines the maximum legal rent. In 2026, homes with up to 143 points count as social housing, with rent capped at €933 a month. Those with 144 to 186 points are regulated midrent, capped at €1,228. Above 186 points, a home is in the free-rental sector, with no maximum rent. How much landlords stand to gain depends on how much the WOZ cap currently limits the rent. In Savills’ example from its report, a fictitious Amsterdam apartment valued at €600K could command an extra €92 a month. The firm’s calculations put the surcharge at €28 to €310 a month and predict the impact to be greatest in Amsterdam, Rotterdam, The Hague and Utrecht, and in other areas with high property values. Former rental homes sold were found to be the most valuable ones, according to Statistics Netherlands. Properties that became owner-occupied had an average WOZ value of €375K, against €327K for all homes let by private landlords. The change was most evident in the G4 cities, where 11% to 15% of individuals’ rental homes moved to the owner-occupied sector over 2024 and 2025. “The adjustment gives landlords of selected homes more rental headroom, but does not fundamentally change the market,” Quint Luiken, commercial manager for asset and property management at Savills, said in a statement. In addition to adjustments to the WWS, the government also wants to extend a 10% rent premium for newly built midrent homes. The premium currently applies to projects that start construction before 2028. The proposal, which has yet to be approved, would push the deadline to Jan. 1, 2032. items.title: Corum Buys Dublin Office And Industrial Portfolio For €100M-Plus
items.description: Courtesy of Deloitte Real Estate Corum has invested more than €100M in its latest Irish deal. French investment manager Corum has agreed to acquire 24 properties at Dublin’s Blanchardstown Corporate Park in a deal worth more than €100M, making it one of Ireland’s largest commercial property transactions of 2026. The portfolio, acquired from Channor Real Estate Group in a deal brokered by Deloitte and Lisney , comprises approximately 370K SF of Grade A office and light industrial accommodation. Blanchardstown Corporate Park has been developed and managed by Channor over the past 30 years, and the wider 100-acre campus contains more than 1M SF of office, industrial and retail accommodation. “There was strong market interest in this portfolio of buildings because they represented a rare opportunity to acquire an established commercial development with long-term and solid commercial potential,” Deloitte Ireland Real Estate Managing Director Dessie Kilkenny said in a statement. Corum AM partner Jonny Smith added that the acquisition would broaden the fund's industrial exposure. “This transaction demonstrates the fund’s continued growth and its ability to acquire sizeable portfolios that offer opportunities across the risk spectrum and broaden its industrial exposure. Transactions of this kind will remain central to the fund’s strategy as it pursues pan-European and transatlantic opportunities,” Smith said in a statement. Blanchardstown Corporate Park was established by the Harrison family in 1996 and is home to more than 200 Irish and international businesses. Recent lettings include a 30,500 SF facility to electrical infrastructure manufacturer Hager, which is using the property as its new Irish headquarters. Channor Real Estate Group CEO Darren Harrison said the deal marked a milestone for the company after three decades developing the business park and described it as a “landmark transaction” and a "testament to the vision and commitment" that had gone into developing Blanchardstown Corporate Park. The acquisition comes as investment activity gathers pace. Investment reached €2.16B in the first nine months of 2026, up 34% on the same period last year, according to Colliers . Industrial and logistics assets attracted €164M across six transactions in the third quarter, while international investors accounted for 87% of total spending. Colliers expects full-year investment to exceed €3B, which would make 2026 the strongest year since 2022. items.title: Service Properties Trust Rejects $2B Cash Bid, Claims Hotel Portfolio Could Be Worth Double
items.description: Service Properties Trust rejected a $2B offer for its hotel portfolio that would have accelerated its plans to transition to a pure-play triple-net lease REIT. Google Maps The Royal Sonesta New Orleans, owned by Service Properties Trust The board, including all six independent trustees, unanimously agreed that offloading the portfolio would not be in the best interests of its shareholders, according to a letter published Friday. Jim Koehler’s TKO made an unsolicited offer for 93 of the REIT’s assets on Oct. 7. The $2B all-cash bid exceeds SVC's entire market capitalization of less than $1B. Rather than taking the offer, the company plans to retain its 77 hotels before selling them starting next year. Service Properties Trust, which is managed by The RMR Group and trades under the ticker SVC, expects that the hotels will grow earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization by approximately $109M within 12 to 24 months, according to the letter. Doing so will allow the REIT to achieve higher sales prices, the board argued. SVC began selling assets in 2025 to pay down debts. In the third quarter, the company reported a net loss of $87.9M , down further from a $46.9M loss during the same period last year. Its funds from operations, a core measure of cash flow for REITs, were $0.31 per share, down from $0.92 a year prior. This year, SVC said it completed 14 of the 15 planned hotel sales for $116.7M combined. It is marketing two more hotels, according to its third-quarter investor presentation. TKO followed up on its offer on Oct. 15 , stating that the investment firm “is prepared to deliver proof of funds demonstrating its strong financial capacity and wherewithal to complete the proposed transaction.” It offered to deposit $50M into escrow to demonstrate its commitment. “Despite submitting an all cash offer, TKO contends that it has received no meaningful response from SVC,” the company said in the statement. “TKO maintains that this silence is difficult to reconcile with SVC's public statements regarding its intention to sell its hotel assets.” SVC originally revealed its rejection in an investor presentation on Nov. 5 , claiming that the $2B offer significantly undervalues the portfolio. Activist Blackwells Capital challenged the decision in a letter published a day later. It argued that RMR's financial ties to hotel operator Sonesta International Hotels create conflicts of interest and that a sale could trigger substantial management termination or transition payments, potentially giving RMR an incentive to resist a deal. The letter, penned by Blackwells Chief Investment Officer Jason Aintabi, highlighted that SVC’s share price is down 85% in five years and 35% in a year. “A board that tells its owners the hotels alone are worth significantly more than $2.0 billion has exactly one legitimate way to prove it: a genuine process, run in the open, by unconflicted trustees," Aintabi said in a statement released alongside the letter. Adjusted hotel EBITDA for SVC’s 77 retained hotels was $41.1M in the third quarter, a 16% increase year-over-year. The REIT said it has invested $628M in those assets since 2023, which has driven an 8% increase in revenue per available room. In its Friday letter responding to Blackwells, the board claimed that the results illustrate that the hotels could be worth between $3B and $4.1B in aggregate. “The Board believes that allowing this growth to take hold before selling offers the opportunity to realize significantly higher proceeds for shareholders than selling the hotels today,” the board wrote. In the last five days, SVC's stock price climbed more than 13%, including 2% between market open and noon on Monday. SVC plans to begin selling the properties individually or in small portfolios and expects to offload all of the properties by the end of 2028. “The Board would seriously consider credible proposals for the Retained Hotels that would accelerate SVC’s transition to a de-levered pure play triple net lease REIT, provided that, in the Board’s judgment, they appropriately value the Retained Hotels and are in the best interests of SVC and all its shareholders,” the board wrote. “TKO’s proposal simply did not meet these standards.” Continue reading this story with a free account Log in or register Related Topics: Blackwells Capital , Jason Aintabi , Net Lease , Service Properties Trust , Sonesta International Hotels , The RMR Group , TKO , Triple Net Lease

items.title: Zara Founder Makes Another Massive Chicago Splash With Gold Coast Apartment Buy
items.description: Billionaire Amancio Ortega , the founder of fashion retailer Zara , reportedly made his second major Chicago acquisition in as many months, dropping more than $200M for a 390-unit apartment tower in Gold Coast. Google Maps 1201 N. LaSalle Drive Ortega's real estate investment arm, Ponte Gadea , acquired The Sinclair at 1201 N. LaSalle Drive on Thursday, CoStar News first reported . The building sale had not yet been finalized in Cook County property records as of the time of publication, but sources told the outlet it was just over $200M. That would make the deal Chicago's highest-priced multifamily trade since Ortega's family office paid $231.5M for the 492-unit apartment building at 727 W. Madison St. in 2023. Ponte Gadea bought The Sinclair from Fifield Cos., which completed the 35-story tower in 2017. It is about 94% leased, with asking rents of roughly $3,800 per unit, according to CoStar. Fifield bought the site for $17.5M in 2015 and took out a $98M construction loan to replace a grocery store. The acquisition comes on the heels of Ortega's bombshell October buy, paying about $550M for the 51-story office tower at 1 N. Wacker Drive. The deal was the year’s third-largest office sale in the country at the time of sale and the largest outright office sale in Chicago since the Aon Center traded for $712M in 2015. Across the three properties, Ortega has invested just under $1B in the city since 2023. Downtown apartment occupancy hit 95.8% in the third quarter, the highest level since 2006, according to Integra Realty Resources. Just over 3,300 apartment units are under construction downtown. items.title: Judge Allows Exton Square Mall Redevelopment To Proceed, Slams 'Absurd' Rejection
items.description: Almost exactly a year after the developer planning a mixed-use mall redevelopment sued a Chester County municipal board for blocking its project, the developer has received permission to move forward. Courtesy of Abrams Realty & Development Judge Sarah Black ruled in favor of Abrams Realty & Development in a Friday decision regarding the future of the now-shuttered Exton Square Mall. She wrote that an "illogical train of thought” led the West Whiteland Board of Supervisors to reject the firm’s master plan application. The developer plans to demolish much of the enclosed shopping center and construct a mixed-use campus including more than 700 residential units and 280K SF of retail. ARD owner Peter Abrams told Bisnow he was glad to see the court rule in his favor and is looking forward to bringing a senior living community, townhomes and new retail space to fruition. While a delivery date for the project remains up in the air, he said if the upcoming permitting process with the township goes smoothly, demolition and construction on the roughly 1M SF project could start as soon as this coming spring. “We are beyond relieved,” Abrams said. “The judge was pretty clear: ‘Don’t screw with these guys anymore,’” he added. The township intends to appeal the decision, West Whiteland Board of Supervisors Chair Brian Dunn told Bisnow on Monday afternoon. He expects the move to be discussed further during the body's Nov. 24 meeting. After being informed of Dunn’s plan to appeal the ruling, Abrams provided another statement to Bisnow . "He ought to think twice, because if he delays us any further we’re going to be back in court and we’re going to be seeking damages," he said. Black found that the board of supervisors — which included just two members at the time of the October 2025 rejection, Dunn and Rajesh Kumbhardare — made faulty rulings on a number of grounds. The board now includes those two members plus a third, Libby Madarasz. The judge knocked the “paradoxical” rejection as vague, contradictory and not backed by hard facts. The board cited concerns about traffic and potential strain on public utilities but also appealed to a broad sense of the project being out of line with constituents’ interests. “There were hundreds of emails from our residents concerning traffic conditions,” Kumbhardare told Bisnow at the time of the rejection . “The density is more than what we would like there to be.” The judge found only four individual objectors in the township’s records of public meetings and concluded that the master plan complied by right with the town center zoning ordinance as it existed at the time of the application. The code was updated shortly thereafter to prevent the amount of density ARD proposed. “This conclusion may be an attempt by the Board to retroactively apply a change in the Township’s density requirements to this particular application,” Black wrote. “It is absurd to demand the Plaintiff explain why compliance with the zoning ordinance is in the best interests of the township,” she added. “Presumably, those ordinances were enacted to effectuate those interests.” Kumbhardare declined Bisnow ’s request for comment and the township’s solicitor, Alex Baumler, didn't respond. The yearlong legal saga has been a financial burden for ARD, which finalized its purchase of the property from PREIT for $34M in March 2025. The developer was forced to carry the largely vacant mall for longer than expected. The vacancy-riddled property shuttered in June . “Holding the property together given the condition that the property is in and continuing to carry it financially was not easy,” Abrams said. “We’ve already been severely damaged financially by these actions.” UPDATE, NOV. 16, 1:30 P.M. recent_coverage.title: Weekley Homes Spends $16M on 38-Acre Dev Site in Scottsdale

recent_coverage.title: ATTOM Reveals July as Best Month to Buy a Home Based on Lowest Premium above AVM

recent_coverage.title: GAMLS: Home prices increase despite overall market slowdown
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Georgia MLS 数据显示，亚特兰大 10 月房价中位数同比上涨 1.3% 至 $395,000；成交量同比下降 19.5%，住宅签约量同比下降 26.8%，在售库存上升 1.4%。

recent_coverage.title: Dermody Adds Tracy Warehouse to West Region Industrial Portfolio
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Dermody 收购 Tracy 一处 606,343 平方英尺的 Class A 物流设施，物业建于 2023 年并可即时入住；交易金额未披露，Colliers 将负责招商。

recent_coverage.title: Monthly Mortgage Payments Fall to Lowest Level in 6 Weeks as Home Prices Keep Dipping
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Redfin 称，截至 11 月 8 日的四周，房价中位数同比下降 0.9% 至 $388,613；按 7.18% 利率计算的月度按揭支付降至 $2,755，但住宅签约量仍处记录低位。

recent_coverage.title: First Look: Construction on AT&T’s New Plano Campus Is Underway
recent_coverage.summary_zh: AT&T 已在 Plano 新总部园区铺设首条光纤并举行奠基仪式；公司预计最早于 2028 年底开始迁入员工，园区建成后可容纳 10,000 人。

recent_coverage.title: Weekly Housing Trends: U.S. Market Update (Week Ending Nov. 7, 2026)
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Realtor.com 表示，截至 11 月 7 日的一周，按揭利率连续三周下降但仍处 7% 以上；新挂牌量已连续六周下降，本周出现两位数跌幅，买卖双方参与度均走弱。

recent_coverage.title: The Generational Housing Divide: Millennials Had It Better Than Baby Boomers–Until the Pandemic Changed the Math
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Redfin 称，疫情后按揭利率从约 3% 升至接近 7%，房价同步上涨；疫情后购房的千禧一代住房支出约占收入 35%，许多人因此被排除在市场之外。

recent_coverage.title: AI borrowers now drive nearly half of long-dated U.S. IG issuance. PIMCO sees 3 diversifiers
recent_coverage.summary_zh: PIMCO 表示，AI 相关借款已占美国非金融投资级债券年初至今、期限超过 15 年发行量的近一半；PIMCO 建议关注机构按揭证券等信用分散资产。

recent_coverage.title: Blackstone Targets $3B Fundraise For Real Estate Secondaries

recent_coverage.title: OCTOBER CHILL BRINGS COOLER SALES, MORE CHOICES FOR HOUSTON BUYERS
recent_coverage.summary_zh: 休斯顿 10 月单户住宅销售同比下降 14.9% 至 6,348 套，中位价下降 3.0% 至 320,000 美元，在售库存同比增加 6.8%。

recent_coverage.title: J.P. Morgan Report, CoreWeave Earnings Provide Positive Signals For Data Center Construction In 2027

recent_coverage.title: Household Debt Delinquencies Rise as Mortgage Performance Weakens
recent_coverage.summary_zh: 纽约联储数据显示，2026 年第三季度约 5.0% 的家庭债务余额处于逾期状态，抵押贷款严重逾期率升至 1.1%，家庭信用压力有所加剧。

recent_coverage.title: Multifamily delinquencies up in October, driven by issues at San Francisco property

recent_coverage.title: High Housing Costs Keep Homeowners Locked-In
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Realtor.com 研究称，典型抵押贷款持有人的本息月供约为 1,300 美元，而按当前市场购房需多支付约 1,100 美元，交易释放仍十分缓慢。

recent_coverage.title: October 2026 Central Texas Housing Report
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Unlock MLS 显示，奥斯汀都会区 10 月成交量同比下降 11.4% 至 2,114 套，中位价下降 6.9% 至 404,802 美元，需求集中于低价房。

recent_coverage.title: BWE Arranges $240M Recapitalization of Midwest Seniors Housing Portfolio
recent_coverage.summary_zh: BWE 为 O’Reilly Development 的老年住房组合安排约 2.4 亿美元资本重组，项目涵盖独立生活、辅助生活和记忆护理社区，入住率为 96% 至 99%。

recent_coverage.title: Clarion Partners Closes $206M Vegas Industrial Buy
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Clarion Partners 收购北拉斯维加斯 130 万平方英尺 A 级工业组合，交易金额为 2.056 亿美元，资产在售出时出租率为 84%。

recent_coverage.title: Institutions Maintain Target Allocations to Real Estate

recent_coverage.title: BNPL for rent seeks a market

recent_coverage.title: Rising appraisal defects signals likely stress for lenders

recent_coverage.title: Year-to-date home-sale growth narrows in Phoenix area with October home-sales dip
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Maricopa County 10 月住宅销售同比下降 18.2% 至 3,214 套，pending sales 下降 46.2% 至 2,147 套，在售住房增加 11.6%。

recent_coverage.title: Affinius Capital Provides $100.3M Construction Loan for Student Housing Project Near University of Pittsburgh
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Affinius Capital 为匹兹堡大学附近 672 床位学生住房项目提供 1.003 亿美元建设贷款，项目计划于 2028 年夏季完工，并含 34 套可负担住房。

recent_coverage.title: October 2026 CPI: Inflation Firms, December Fed Hike Looms
